subject: Clarifying PHI handling & BAA for Cascade Health integration
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elenam@cascade-health.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-03-21T09:17:00-04:00
Subject: Quick question on PHI/BAA — is Redwood eligible?

Hi Grace,

We're kicking off an internal review for a pilot using Redwood to generate clinical summaries. Before we set up an eval, our security and legal teams asked whether Redwood will sign a BAA and whether the hosted API can be used with PHI.

High-level: pilot volume ~5k patient messages/month, data will contain limited identifiers (name, MRN) and clinical notes.

Can you confirm:
- Do you sign BAAs for hosted customers?
- If hosted is not eligible, do you offer Dedicated or private options that support PHI?
- Any constraints on retention, logging, or subprocessors we should know about?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

Elena
Director, IT Security
Cascade Health

---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elenam@cascade-health.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-03-21T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI/BAA — is Redwood eligible?

Hi Elena — thanks for the details and the heads-up on volume. Short answer: we do sign BAAs, but eligibility depends on deployment mode and a few controls. Looping in Monica (legal) and Vivek (security) to confirm the exact scope and required evidence.

Immediate notes:
- Hosted API: supported with a BAA in our Dedicated/Private offerings — hosted (multi-tenant) generally not recommended for PHI unless customer has an approved data flow; we'll need to review the exact integration pattern.
- Dedicated: recommended for predictable throughput and isolation; can be provisioned in your preferred region.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): available for highly regulated setups if required.

I'll ask legal for the BAA template and security for SOC2/architecture artifacts. If you can share the expected integration (API direct vs. proxying through your VPC) that will speed this up.

Regards,
Grace
Account Executive — Healthcare
Redwood Inference

---
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elenam@cascade-health.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-03-22T08:41:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI/BAA — is Redwood eligible?

Hi Elena — Monica from legal. Thanks for the context. A couple of clarifying questions so we can scope a BAA and confirm eligibility:

1) Which Redwood service do you plan to use: Hosted API (redwood-hosted), Dedicated (customer-dedicated pool), or Private (VPC/on-prem)?
2) Do you intend to send raw identifiers (SSNs, full DOB) or only name/MRN + clinical text?
3) Expected retention/archival needs (e.g., retain logs for X days, or require deletion on request)?
4) Is Cascade using a proxy in your VPC or calling Redwood directly from your application?

For Hosted (multi-tenant): our standard position is to support non-PHI use cases. We will consider PHI on a case-by-case basis with compensating controls (TLS+mutual auth, dedicated tenancy, contractual commitments). For Dedicated/Private: we can include PHI in scope and execute a BAA.

I'll attach a redlineable BAA template and our SOC 2 summary so you can share with your legal/security reviewers. Once we confirm deployment mode and retention, we'll prepare a final BAA and a DocuSign send.

Best,
Monica
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

---
From: Elena Morales <elenam@cascade-health.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-03-22T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI/BAA — is Redwood eligible?

Hi Monica — thanks. Answers below:
- Deployment: prefer Hosted for ease of ops; if Hosted requires extra controls we're open to Dedicated.
- Data: names, MRNs, DOB (limited), and clinical notes. No SSNs.
- Retention: logs need to be retained 90 days; clinical data should be deletable on request and not stored beyond 30 days unless explicitly archived by us.
- Integration: calls will originate from our app servers in AWS us-east-1 (no VPC peering initially).

If Hosted is acceptable with the right contractual and technical guarantees, that's ideal. Otherwise please outline what's required to provision Dedicated.

Elena

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elenam@cascade-health.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-03-22T11:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI/BAA — is Redwood eligible?

Hi Elena — Vivek from Security. Thank you for the clear answers. Technical summary & next steps: 

1) Hosted eligibility:
- Multi-tenant hosted APIs are not our default for PHI unless we agree to dedicated tenancy and specific contractual limits. Given Cascade's plan to call from app servers (no VPC), we can offer a logically isolated tenancy layer (customer-dedicated model instances + strict routing) but require Dedicated for guaranteed isolation and SLA.

2) Dedicated option:
- We can provision a Dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1. That gives separate tenant allocation, configurable retention, and no shared KV caches across tenants.
- Network: we support secure egress + optional customer-managed VPN or VPC peering if you want to avoid public internet.

3) Controls we provide and evidence:
- Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at-rest with KMS-managed keys.
- Audit logs (access and admin) retained configurable up to 365 days — default 90 days. We can set log retention to 90 days to match your requirement.
- PHI handling: we do not use customer data for model training by default; we can contractually prohibit it and document the data flow.
- Subprocessors: list available; we'll provide current subprocessors and SOC 2 summary.

I've attached: redwood_SOC2_type2_summary.pdf, BAA_template_redwood.docx, network_diagram_v1.pdf (attachment stubs in this thread). Also including a short checklist for provisioning Dedicated.

Next steps:
- If Dedicated is acceptable, confirm commitment window so we can provision capacity (typically 3–5 business days for a standard pool).
- Legal to exchange and finalize the BAA.

Happy to do a technical call to walk through the network diagram.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
From: Elena Morales <elenam@cascade-health.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-03-22T12:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI/BAA — is Redwood eligible?

Vivek/Monica — thanks, that is helpful. Dedicated sounds like the safer route. A few quick clarifications before we proceed:
- Can you confirm deletion semantics: if we request deletion, will cached KV entries and logs be purged within 72 hours?
- Does Redwood accept customer-managed KMS keys for data-at-rest encryption?
- Please send the subprocessors list and a SOC2 report (summary ok for now) so I can share with our procurement team.

If answers look good, we'll ask procurement to approve a Dedicated pilot and expect to sign the BAA. Please also send a DocuSign link when the BAA is ready.

Elena

---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elenam@cascade-health.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-03-22T15:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI/BAA — is Redwood eligible?

Hi Elena — quick follow-up and next steps from our side:
- Deletion: yes — we can configure deletion of KV caches and short-term logs within 72 hours as part of the Dedicated pilot; we'll include the SLA in the BAA.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for Dedicated and Private deployments; we'll include that option in the configuration form.
- Subprocessors & SOC2: attaching a SOC2 summary and current subprocessors list (see attachments).

I'll have Monica prepare a redlineable BAA and send a DocuSign envelope this afternoon (you should see a link from DocuSign in the related links). Once signed we'll kick off provisioning — target provisioning lead time: 3–5 business days after signature and billing setup.

Thanks — happy to schedule a tech call if you'd like a walkthrough of the network diagram.

Best,
Grace
Account Executive — Healthcare
Redwood Inference
